item.description: He made the comment during a visit to the historic Afro-Peruvian city of Zaña, a UNESCO-recognised memorial site for slavery.

item.title: Africanews: South Sudan postpones first general election from December to February
item.description: The elections commission says this will allow for the implementation of additional processes including distribution of registration materials and civic education.

item.title: Africanews: DR Congo: Ebola-awareness campaigns conducted at schools in Bunia
item.description: About 40 schools in the province have reported cases of Ebola since classes resumed in September, with one teacher dying of the disease.

item.title: BBC Africa: My mother told me I would die if I sought treatment for Ebola - I am proof you can survive
item.description: Fear and misinformation surrounds the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo - Dr Kamwanga's mother was not immune.

item.title: BBC Africa: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
item.description: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.

item.title: BBC Africa: Nigeria cautions against travel via Ethiopia's main airport due to altitude
item.description: The foreign ministry in Abuja says 6 Nigerians with underlying health problems have died this year while transiting through Addis Ababa.

item.title: Africanews: World Diabetes Day: South African health leaders urge early action to detect the disease
item.description: The health minister said the condition is now the country's number one killer, taking the top spot from HIV/AIDS.

item.title: Africanews: Microsoft apologises for global outage and rules out cyberattack
item.description: The tech giant said on Saturday that service has now been restored across Teams, Outlook, and its other products, ending the shutdown.

item.title: Africanews: Burkina Faso issues arrest warrants for around 20 people, including journalists
item.description: The warrants target exiled journalists, activists, an ex-minister, and former military officers who face several terrorism-related charges.

item.title: Africanews: United States nationwide ground stop lifted after longest shutdown since 2001
item.description: The over four-hour stoppage on Friday brought all air travel to a halt across the country and stranded tens of thousands of passengers.

item.title: BBC Africa: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
item.description: Jojo was poached as an infant and grew up in captivity. His keepers want to find him a friend - but it's not straightforward.

item.title: BBC Africa: E Guinea goalkeeper involved in fatal collision gets 12-game ban
item.description: Jesus Owono is given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee after his challenge which resulted in the death of Jesus de Miguel.

item.title: Africanews: DR Congo: At least 44 dead in attack by Islamic State-linked gunmen
item.description: The latest raids by the Allied Democratic Forces come just days after the notoriously brutal group killed 66 people in North Kivu.

item.title: Africanews: South Sudanese start registering to vote ahead of first national elections
item.description: The voter registration operation runs until 28 November ahead of the polls which have been postponed several times since independence in 2011.

item.title: BBC Africa: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever
item.description: The 52-year-old general’s provocative posts and military threats have fuelled rumours of a dynastic succession.

item.title: BBC Africa: Oranges investigated after four girls die in suspected Uganda school poisoning
item.description: The girls started vomiting after eating oranges brought in by a fellow pupil - police are travelling to the village they came from.

item.title: Africanews: France escalates Algeria trade dispute to EU-level
item.description: France on Friday asked the European Commission to look into Algeria’s alleged non-compliance with a EU trade deal. Paris is accusing Algers of an almost total blockade on French imports and of suspending urea shipments to France.

item.title: Africanews: CAR: Opposition marches in Bangui against rising cost of living
item.description: Hundreds of people took to the streets of Bangui on Friday to protest the rising cost of living in Central African Republic and the arrest of five civil society leaders.

item.title: Africanews: Burkinabe authorities vow to support gold miners expelled from Guinea
item.description: Since November 6, thousands of Burkinabe gold miners have been returning home. In Bobo-Dioulasso, more than 37,000 Burkinabe nationals, including some 8,000 children, as well as more than a thousand citizens of other nationalities, are hoping to start a new life with support from the authorities.

item.title: BBC Africa: Arokodare double secures Nigeria win in Afcon 2027 qualifier
item.description: Tolu Arokodare scores twice in the second half as Nigeria claim a 3-1 win over Tanzania to bolster their hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

item.title: BBC Africa: Ghana kick-start Afcon 2027 bid despite Ayew penalty miss
item.description: Ghana kick-start their Afcon 2027 qualifying campaign despite Jordan Ayew having a penalty saved, while Cameroon, Ivory Coast and Senegal register wins.

item.title: Africanews: Teddy Riner announces presidential bid, pledges to unite France
item.description: In an interview with Le Parisien, Riner said he could not remain silent amid growing social tensions and uncertainty about France's future.

item.title: Africanews: São Tomé's president reappoints PM following legislative elections
item.description: Américo Ramos' party came a close second in the polls, but the winning party, the Movement for the Liberation of São Tomé and Príncipe, failed to win additional support.
